questions.title: Print Hello, World!
questions.description:
Write a function `hello()` that returns the string `Hello, World!`.

Example:
- hello() -> "Hello, World!"

questions.title: Add Two Numbers
questions.description:
Write a function `add(a, b)` that returns the sum of two numbers.

Example:
- add(2, 3) -> 5
questions.reference_solution:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

questions.title: Sum 1 to N
questions.description:
Write a function `sum_to_n(n)` that returns the sum of all integers from 1 to n (inclusive) using a loop.

Example:
- sum_to_n(5) -> 15

questions.title: Is Even
questions.description:
Write a function `is_even(n)` that returns `True` if n is even and `False` otherwise.

Example:
- is_even(4) -> True

questions.title: Maximum of Two
questions.description:
Write a function `max_of_two(a, b)` that returns the larger of two numbers.

Example:
- max_of_two(3, 8) -> 8
questions.reference_solution:
def max_of_two(a, b):
    return a if a > b else b

questions.title: Count Vowels
questions.description:
Write a function `count_vowels(s)` that returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in the string s (lowercase only).

Example:
- count_vowels("hello") -> 2
questions.reference_solution:
def count_vowels(s):
    return sum(1 for c in s if c in 'aeiou')

questions.title: Reverse a String
questions.description:
Write a function `reverse_string(s)` that returns the string s reversed.

Example:
- reverse_string("abc") -> "cba"

questions.title: Factorial
questions.description:
Write a function `factorial(n)` that returns n! (the product of all integers from 1 to n). factorial(0) is 1.

Example:
- factorial(5) -> 120

questions.title: FizzBuzz Value
questions.description:
Write a function `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns:
- "FizzBuzz" if n is divisible by both 3 and 5,
- "Fizz" if divisible by 3,
- "Buzz" if divisible by 5,
- otherwise the number n as a string.

Example:
- fizzbuzz(15) -> "FizzBuzz"

questions.title: Count to N (list)
questions.description:
Write a function `count_to_n(n)` that returns a list of integers from 1 to n using a loop.

Example:
- count_to_n(3) -> [1, 2, 3]
